1. Updated Data Model Design (Conceptual Entity-Relationship)To resolve the one-to-many relationship between bulk purchases and recipe usage, the database architecture is normalized into three distinct entities. This ensures a single source of truth for pricing while allowing infinite flexibility in recipe formulation.Entity 1: Bulk Ingredient MasterActs as the parent record, storing only the financial cost of the physical bulk item.Primary Key: Ingredient IDAttributes: Ingredient Name (e.g., Sugar), Purchase Unit (e.g., 1 kg), Purchase Price (e.g., Php 80.00).   Entity 2: Recipe Unit Conversions (One-to-Many Child)Stores the multiple ways a single parent ingredient can be measured in a kitchen.Primary Key: Conversion IDForeign Key: Ingredient ID (Links to Parent)Attributes: Recipe Unit (e.g., cup, grams, tbs), Yield Factor (e.g., 5, 1000, 80).   Entity 3: Recipe Line Item (Transactional)Captures the exact usage for a specific batch formula.Primary Key: Line Item IDForeign Keys: Recipe ID, Ingredient ID, Conversion ID. (Linking the exact unit variation chosen).Attributes: Batch Quantity (e.g., 0.25, 50, 1).   2. End-to-End Technical WorkflowThe system workflow is divided into three distinct operational phases to ensure data integrity from data entry to final calculation.Phase A: Master Data Initialization (Setup)Bulk Entry: The user navigates to the Ingredient Master and logs a new physical purchase (e.g., Sugar, 1 kg, Php 80.00).   Yield Rule Definition: Within the same interface, the user defines multiple yield parameters for that specific ingredient.Hierarchy Commit: The system saves the parent item and links the three distinct conversion rules (cup = 5 yield, grams = 1000 yield, tbs = 80 yield) to it in the database.   Phase B: Recipe Formulation (Data Binding)Line Item Creation: The user adds a new ingredient row in the Recipe Builder dashboard.Parent Selection: The user selects "Sugar" from the primary ingredient list.Cascading Filter: The frontend instantly queries the backend for the conversion rules tied specifically to "Sugar".Unit Selection: The secondary "Unit" dropdown dynamically populates with only valid options (cup, grams, tbs). The user selects "grams".   Quantity Input: The user inputs the required batch quantity (e.g., 50).   Phase C: Cost Engine Resolution (Execution)Data Retrieval: The backend calculation engine identifies the exact Conversion ID selected by the user.Normalization: The engine divides the parent Purchase Price (Php 80.00) by the selected Yield Factor (1000).   Unit Cost Output: The system resolves the micro-cost (Php 0.08 per gram).   Batch Line Cost: The engine multiplies the unit cost by the batch quantity (Php 0.08 × 50 grams) to finalize the line item cost at Php 4.00.   Aggregation: This resolved line item is summed into the Total Variable Cost, triggering the rest of the profitability formulas.3. UI/UX Interaction DesignThe graphical interface requires specific structural changes to accommodate this hierarchical data without confusing the user.Ingredient Master Module:Design Pattern: Master-Detail View.Layout: The main form captures the bulk details. Below this, a dynamic sub-grid (inline editable table) allows the user to click "Add Conversion Rule" to infinitely stack new unit/yield combinations under the same parent ingredient.Recipe Builder Module:Design Pattern: Cascading Selectors.Layout: The traditional static "Unit" text field is replaced with a dependent dropdown menu. It remains disabled and grayed out until the user selects a primary ingredient. Once an ingredient is chosen, the dropdown activates and strictly limits the user to the units defined in Phase A, eliminating manual data entry errors or invalid unit selections.4. Backend-to-Frontend Communication ContractThe Inter-Process Communication (IPC) between the Rust backend and the React frontend must transfer hierarchical data efficiently to power the cascading dropdowns.Initialization Payload: When the Recipe Builder loads, the backend must send a nested data structure. It transmits the list of all parent ingredients, and inside each parent object, it includes an array of all associated conversion rules (ID, Unit Name, Yield Factor).State Management: The frontend stores this nested list in memory. When the user changes the parent ingredient dropdown, the frontend instantly swaps out the array supplying the secondary unit dropdown without needing to query the database a second time, ensuring zero latency during recipe formulation.
